programs.name: Full Ramadan Fast
programs.description: Experience fasting as Muslims do during Ramadan - from the pre-dawn suhoor until sunset iftar. This is the authentic Ramadan experience.
tips: Suhoor is essential - never skip it
Break your fast gently with dates and water
Listen to your body throughout the day

programs.name: Gentle Start
programs.description: Perfect for those new to fasting. Start with a comfortable 12-hour window, similar to overnight fasting most people already do naturally.
tips: Start eating earlier in the evening before your first fast
Include protein-rich foods in your suhoor

programs.name: Building Strength
programs.description: For those with some fasting experience. This mirrors popular 16:8 intermittent fasting protocols used for wellness.
tips: Plan your meals carefully to maximize nutrition
Consider light activity during fasting hours
Use this time for reflection and mindfulness

sunnahFasting.title: Voluntary Fasting in Islamic Tradition
sunnahFasting.description: Beyond Ramadan, there are recommended voluntary fasts throughout the year that Muslims may observe.

types.name: Monday & Thursday Fasting
types.description: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) used to fast on Mondays and Thursdays. He explained that deeds are presented to Allah on these days.

types.name: Ayyam al-Beed
types.description: Fasting on the 13th, 14th, and 15th of each Islamic lunar month, called the 'white days' due to the full moon.

types.name: Day of Arafah
types.description: Fasting on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah (for non-pilgrims) is highly recommended and believed to expiate sins.

types.name: Six Days of Shawwal
types.description: Fasting six days in the month following Ramadan. Combined with Ramadan, it's equivalent to fasting the entire year.
